**AG-UI** (Agent–User Interaction Protocol) is an **open, lightweight, event-based standard** designed to connect AI agents to user-facing applications across web, mobile, terminals, and chat platforms.[1]

***

## Core Purpose

Traditional request-and-response architectures (like standard REST or GraphQL APIs) struggle with agentic workflows that require multi-turn streaming, shared state, client-side actions, and human intervention.[1]

AG-UI standardizes how agent runtime events, UI intents, and user interactions flow bidirectionally between backends and frontends without ad-hoc custom wiring.[1]

***

## The Agentic Protocol Ecosystem

AG-UI is part of a broader standard stack for agentic computing:[1]

| Layer | Protocol / Standard | Focus & Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Agent ↔ User** | **AG-UI** | Connects agents to user interfaces for real-time interaction and state [1]. |
| **Agent ↔ Tools & Data** | **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) | Connects agents securely to external databases, tools, and APIs [1]. |
| **Agent ↔ Agent** | **A2A** (Agent to Agent) | Orchestrates distributed coordination across distinct agents [1]. |

***

## Key Capabilities & Features

- **Streaming and Multimodality:** Real-time token and event streaming, typed file attachments, voice, and media playback.[1]
- **Generative UI:** Delivers structured outputs to render typed UI components or declarative interface trees.[1]
- **Shared State:** Synchronizes typed state bidirectionally between the user interface and backend using event diffs.[1]
- **Human-in-the-Loop Interrupts:** Supports pausing executions for user approvals, manual edits, or steerable interventions mid-flow.[1]
- **Frontend & Backend Tooling:** Manages typed execution handoffs between agent backend tools and client-side actions.[1]

***

## Supported Ecosystem & Integrations

The protocol was originated by the team behind CopilotKit and supports a wide range of frameworks and environments:[1]

- **Frameworks:** LangGraph, CrewAI, Agno, Pydantic AI, Mastra, LlamaIndex, AG2, Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, and Claude Managed Agents.[1]
- **Infrastructure:** Native deployment support in runtimes such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.[2]
- **SDKs & Clients:** Multi-language SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin, Dart) and client integrations spanning Web, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and CLI terminals.[1]

Interactive examples, code walkthroughs, and templates are available on the AG-UI Dojo and Official Documentation.[1]
